newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee recovering after sharp fall vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee recovering after sharp fall vs dollar.

text.p: The rupee recovered to 35.84/85 after dipping to 35.86/87 earlier on Thursday as dollar demand from the state-run Bank of Baroda was exhausted, dealers said.
They said the bank, not usually a large player in the inter-bank market, hit the market at the 35.81 level and pushed the dollar up to 35.86.
The rupee opened the day steady at 35.80/81.
According to speculation doing the rounds of dealing rooms, the bank was buying dollars on behalf of an oil firm -- many believed the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation.
Bankers have suggested in recent weeks that oil firms routing dollar purchases through the inter-bank market would help correct the overvalued rupee and boost exporters' morale.
"We don't know if it is a one-off event or a precursor to the oil price hike," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"If it happens consistently, we could see a pattern."
Forward dollar premiums edged down as exporters, attracted by rising dollar, were keen sellers, a dealer said.
